objectives.trace-authentication: Trace a claimed identity through credential verification to an authenticated actor.
objectives.evaluate-access: Evaluate an access decision for an actor, action and resource using authoritative policy inputs.
objectives.distinguish-actors: Distinguish the represented actor, the request sender and the principal used by Spring Security.
objectives.assign-responsibility: Explain who verifies proof, who asserts identity and who guards the protected resource.
objectives.compare-request-paths: Compare human and workload requests and diagnose a denial without expanding permissions.

sections.title: Separate an identity from its proof

practice.prompt: Maya types her account name but has not supplied a password. What has the dashboard learned?

choices.label: The account being claimed.
choices.reason: The name identifies the account to look up. The verifier still needs evidence tied to that account.

choices.label: That Maya controls the account.
choices.reason: Anyone can type a known account name. That does not establish control.

choices.label: That Maya can read North tasks.
choices.reason: The dashboard has neither verified the caller nor evaluated the requested operation.

sections.title: Name the actor at each boundary

practice.prompt: The verifier rejects the dashboard’s password and no trusted caller is established. Where is the failure?

choices.label: The action policy.
choices.reason: That policy evaluates an actor and operation. This request has not established its actor yet.

choices.label: Authentication.
choices.reason: Identity evidence did not pass verification. Changing a permission would leave that failure in place.

choices.label: The task’s workspace scope.
choices.reason: Scope matters once policy can evaluate a verified actor against the actual task. It cannot repair failed proof.

sections.title: Decide access to a specific resource

practice.prompt: Maya has a verified identity and task:read. She requests a task stored in South, but her membership is North. What should the policy do?

choices.label: Allow because task:read is present.
choices.reason: The grant satisfies the action check. The stored task still has to belong to her workspace.

choices.label: Deny because South is outside Maya’s scope.
choices.reason: Authentication succeeded and the action is allowed in principle. This resource is outside the scope of the rule.

choices.label: Ask Maya to authenticate again.
choices.reason: There is no evidence of failed verification. Signing in again does not change resource scope.

sections.title: Follow a person and a workload

practice.prompt: An overnight job runs without a user. Which identity should appear as the caller of the task API?

choices.label: The person who deployed the job.
choices.reason: Deployment ownership is useful audit context. It does not establish which actor made this request.

choices.label: The job’s verified workload identity.
choices.reason: Correct. Authenticate the actor actually making the request and give it only the operation and resource scope it needs.

choices.label: Whichever user last opened the dashboard.
choices.reason: The scheduled job and the dashboard session are independent. Reusing a user identity blurs permission and audit boundaries.

claim-and-proof.title: From identity to an authenticated principal

items.label: Identity
items.detail: The account or workload represented in the system.

items.label: Claimed identity
items.detail: The caller says which account it is using.

items.label: Credential or evidence
items.detail: Something a verifier can check against that claim.

items.label: Authentication
items.detail: The verifier checks the evidence under the configured rules.

items.label: Authenticated principal
items.detail: The application’s representation of the verified actor for this interaction.

access-path.title: Authentication and authorization in one request

items.label: Caller
items.detail: Maya opens the dashboard.

items.label: Credentials
items.detail: The dashboard submits evidence for the claimed account.

items.label: Verification
items.detail: The verifier checks the evidence. If it fails, this path stops.

items.label: Authenticated principal
items.detail: The application can now identify its caller.

items.label: Access policy
items.detail: Evaluate the authenticated actor, requested action, actual task and its workspace.

items.label: Allow or deny
items.detail: Permit a North task with read authority. Deny a South task even after authentication succeeds.

items.label: Trusted inputs
items.detail: Grants and membership come from trusted data. The workspace on the task comes from storage.

items.label: Permission check
items.detail: canRead is true only when the grants contain task:read.

items.label: Scope check
items.detail: inScope is true only when the stored task and actor workspace match.

items.label: Final decision
items.detail: The method returns true only when both checks pass.

policy-outcomes.title: Change one input at a time

items.label: Allow · task:read
items.detail: Action permitted and task is in North.

items.label: Deny · task:create only
items.detail: Task is in North, but the read action is missing.

items.label: Deny · task:read
items.detail: The action is permitted, but the task is in South.

items.label: Receive identity evidence
items.detail: The sign-in endpoint or entry component accepts the claim and its proof.

items.label: Validate evidence
items.detail: A verifier checks it or the application validates a statement from a trusted provider.

items.label: Establish the actor
items.detail: Use the verified account or trusted assertion to establish the principal.

items.label: Evaluate access policy
items.detail: Look up the actual resource and compare its scope with the actor’s trusted grants.

items.label: Enforce the decision
items.detail: The resource boundary returns the protected task only when policy allows it.

items.label: Runtime actor
items.detail: Maya’s verified account.

items.label: Evidence
items.detail: Sign-in proof, followed by a validated session in this design.

items.label: Policy input
items.detail: Maya’s trusted membership and task:read.

items.label: Runtime actor
items.detail: The exporter’s verified workload identity.

items.label: Evidence
items.detail: Proof provisioned to the exporter for its own identity.

items.label: Policy input
items.detail: The exporter’s separately assigned grants and workspace scope.
